about.title: Imperial Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Imperial is a small community, and a fatal collision here can shake an entire family and neighborhood at once. While recent public crash data for Imperial shows collisions concentrated on corridors like Rt 86, Aten Road, 2nd Street, and Clark Road, with Friday midday hours seeing more reported activity, any single fatal crash changes everything for the people left behind. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim against the party responsible. These claims are separate from any criminal proceeding and focus on the losses your family carries forward: funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their guidance, love, and companionship. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect Imperial families with an independent personal injury attorney who can explain what a claim might look like for your specific situation, with no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Imperial Families Should Understand About These Claims

items.title: Who Can File Matters
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people, usually a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. An attorney can help clarify where you and your family stand.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You'd Expect
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim in California, and that window shrinks considerably if a government entity, like a public road agency, may be involved. Waiting to get informed can cost your family options.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: A wrongful death claim isn't only about funeral costs or lost income; California law also recognizes the loss of a loved one's companionship, guidance, and love as compensable losses. An independent attorney can help explain how these are typically evaluated.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in Imperial?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children typically have first priority to file. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may qualify. An independent attorney can review your family's specific circumstances to clarify who has standing.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a road like Rt 86 or Aten Road?
items.answer: The specific road matters mainly for gathering evidence, such as public collision records and any relevant traffic patterns, including the Friday midday hours when Imperial has seen more reported crash activity. It doesn't change your family's legal rights, but it can shape how an attorney investigates the case.

items.question: How long do we have to take action after losing a family member?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. That period can be significantly shorter if a government entity is a potential defendant, so it's worth speaking with an independent attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to any criminal charges against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on compensating the family, regardless of whether criminal charges are filed or how they're resolved. The two processes run on different tracks with different purposes and timelines.
